text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Justice Minister Sevket Kazan stops the reading in his office of a joint press release by 14 pro-Islamist organisations because their statement targeted the military.
- The Turkish navy commander sees an Islamic coup as more of a danger than the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan pays two critical visits on Monday night to the National Security Council and the Turkish Intelligence Service, which criticise anti-secular movements.
- The U.S. embassy in Ankara says the United States is considering inviting Prime Minister Erbakan for a visit and says it is pleased with State Minister Abdullah Gul's trip.
- Iran's Foreign Ministry protests at anti-Iranian statements by the deputy chief of the Turkish armed forces on his visit to the United States.
- There are widespread rumours of deputies tranferring parties in parliament, with the ruling coalition gearing up to attract deputies from the opposition.
- Sweeping steps are taken to turn the Turkish Cypriot economy into a new Hong Kong.
- Turkish Cypriots will move into the Cypriot ghost town of Varosha, or Marash in Turkish, if Greek Cypriots pay the first installment for Russian S-300 anti-aircraft missiles.
